title: India Runs More Military Exercises With US Than Any Other Country
excerpt: A US fact sheet on the Major Defense Partnership catalogues a 2026 calendar spanning Yudh Abhyas, Tarang Shakti, Tiger Triumph and Malabar, alongside the Javelin deal and a first Quad joint exercise planned for 2027.
body:
• India conducts more military exercises with the United States than with any other country, according to a US fact sheet titled "US-India Major Defense Partnership" reported by ANI on November 23.
  • The 2026 exercise calendar spanned Yudh Abhyas in Uttarakhand and Rajasthan, Tarang Shakti at Jodhpur — the first exercise on Indian soil to include US F-35 jets — Tiger Triumph at Visakhapatnam and the Quad's Malabar off Japan.
  • Industrial ties deepened in parallel: an August agreement to buy Javelin anti-tank missiles, a Lockheed Martin-Raytheon-Tata MoU to explore co-producing them in India, and a $45 million Boeing contract for the Navy's P-8I fleet.
  • At the Quad leaders' summit in Manila this month, the four countries announced their first-ever joint military exercise, planned for 2027 alongside Sea Dragon.

India now trains alongside the United States more than with any other military on Earth. That is the headline finding of a US fact sheet titled "US-India Major Defense Partnership," reported by ANI on November 23, which catalogues a year of exercises, defence sales and co-production deals built on the 10-year framework the two countries signed in 2025.

"The United States and India share a strong and growing Major Defense Partnership built on trust, mutual respect, and shared security interests," the fact sheet stated. US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor made the same point aboard the aircraft carrier USS George Washington last week: "India conducts more military exercises with the United States than with any other nation on Earth, forging interoperability across land, sea, and air that cannot be improvised in a crisis," Gor said, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

A full calendar across land, air and sea

The 22nd edition of Exercise Yudh Abhyas ran from September 15 to 27 across Auli in Uttarakhand and the Mahajan Field Firing Range in Rajasthan, with approximately 500-600 personnel from each country training in integrated combat operations, counterterrorism, drones, autonomous systems and live fire. Days later, the Indian Air Force's multinational Exercise Tarang Shakti ran from September 26 to October 12 at Jodhpur, where American F-35 fifth-generation fighters took part in a military exercise on Indian soil for the first time, alongside six other foreign air forces.

The fifth edition of the tri-service Exercise Tiger Triumph followed from October 31 to November 5 at Visakhapatnam, focused on humanitarian assistance and disaster relief, amphibious operations and staff planning; Gor noted that the two forces integrated operational cyber elements during Tiger Triumph for the first time. The Quad navies then exercised together in Malabar 2026, held from November 5 to 12 in Japan — an exercise that began as a bilateral US-India drill in 1992 and now involves all four Quad partners. Maritime logistics ties also advanced on November 20, when the US Navy's Military Sealift Command vessel USNS Wally Schirra arrived at Larsen & Toubro's Kattupalli shipyard near Chennai for maintenance under the US-India Master Ship Repair Agreement, as detailed in the ANI report carried by Desi Talk.

"There are many countries that the United States works with. There are only a few we truly trust, and India is one of them."

— Sergio Gor, US Ambassador to India

Deals and co-production

On March 27, India signed a $45 million contract with Boeing India Defense Private Limited for maintenance and inspection of the Indian Navy's US-built P-8I maritime patrol aircraft. In August, the two countries signed an agreement for India's purchase of American-made Javelin anti-tank guided missile systems, and on August 30 Lockheed Martin and Raytheon signed a memorandum of understanding with Tata Advanced Systems Limited to explore co-production of Javelin missiles in India. Senior-level traffic matched the hardware: Admiral Samuel J. Paparo, Commander of US Indo-Pacific Command, visited India in February and again in October, and a US delegation drawn from five combatant commands attended the annual Military Cooperation Group talks in November.

The Quad widens

At the Quad Foreign Ministers' Meeting in New Delhi in May, the four countries announced an Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration initiative, and ministers reviewed the Quad-at-Sea Ship Observer Mission and the Indo-Pacific Logistics Network in Atlanta on October 31. At the Quad Leaders' Summit in Manila this month, President Donald Trump joined the leaders of India, Australia and Japan to announce the grouping's first-ever joint military exercise, scheduled for 2027 in conjunction with Exercise Sea Dragon, bringing together maritime patrol aircraft including the P-8 and P-3C from all four countries.
